scope_accused_affected: GENERAL - all 187 accused; specifically named: 2 (A-1, A-187)
contentions_and_observations: The reasoned cognizance order. SFIO's case: the MCA ordered investigation into 125 Adarsh Group companies and LLPs under s.212(1)(c) Companies Act 2013; the investigation report of 09.05.2019 is deemed a police report under s.173 CrPC by virtue of s.212(15). The accused were categorised 1-5 by control and ownership. SFIO submitted that Mukesh Modi and his family and associates were in direct or indirect control of the corporate entities to the degree of being their 'directing mind and will', acting in connivance with the other accused; that 54 companies and their directors were liable under s.58A(5) of the 1956 Act for the period to 31.03.2014; and that Abhay K Shah & Associates was statutory auditor of the group with Abhay K Shah, Ichchhita Dungarwal and Neha Kataria as signing partners. Court found sufficient prima facie evidence against A-1 to A-187 and set out offence-wise liability.
what_the_order_decided: Detailed 73-page cognizance order giving reasons for the summoning order of the same date; sets out offence-wise liability under the Companies Act 2013 (ss.447, 447 r/w 36, 147, 448) and IPC ss.120B, 418, 420 against each accused and group of companies.

Court kept the reply under consideration.

Jail Superintendent's explanation for handing over custody taken on record and kept under consideration for 01.07.2019; SHO directed to produce the accused on that date.

contentions_and_observations: The first substantial contest on personal appearance. Bailable warrants were served but none of the accused appeared; instead they moved separate applications under s.205 CrPC seeking exemption on grounds of medical problems or personal reasons. SFIO opposed vehemently, calling the grounds false and fabricated. Court held that irrespective of the individual grounds there was no basis in fact or law for exemption, because the accused stood summoned for a non-bailable offence under the Companies Act 2013 triable as a warrant case; they were required to surrender and seek regular bail, and non-bailable warrants could even have been issued given the gravity of the allegations. SFIO also explained the group structures, so that A-1 to A-70 would be served through A-123, A-71 to A-78 through A-135, and the Harivyasi companies through A-115.
what_the_order_decided: Composite order dealing with all 187 accused individually and by group. Fixes how the accused companies are to be served and represented through their authorised representatives u/s 305 CrPC (A-1 to A-70 through A-123 Rohit Modi; A-71 to A-78 through A-135 Sidharath Chauhan; A-79, A-90 to A-93 through A-115 Vivek Harivyasi). Complaint and supporting record, including a pen drive, directed to be supplied to all appearing accused. Adjourned to 13.08.2019.

contentions_and_observations: Defence for Surender Singh (A-140) argued that Akshat Singh, the other director of the same companies A-81 and A-82, faced identical allegations, so his bail should await Akshat Singh's appearance; SFIO did not oppose and sought to verify issues. Court agreed that bail pleas within a set of companies would be similar and deciding one would affect the others, and adjourned. Another accused argued there was no summoning order against him under s.447 for violation of ss.73 and 74 read with the proviso to s.76-A. The core question identified for the group of bail applications was whether an offence under s.448 punishable under s.447 was made out against directors who had signed the account books without mala fide intention.
what_the_order_decided: Bail applications of Surender Singh (A-140) and Jainam Rathod (A-130) adjourned to 20.08.2019, interim bail extended. A-113, A-114 and A-117 remanded to judicial custody on expiry of remand; A-115 remanded after production by video conferencing. A-120, A-122, A-123, A-125, A-126, A-131, A-134 and A-142 taken into custody in this case and remanded till 27.08.2019.

Separately, an exemption application was dismissed on the ground that the accused stood summoned for non-bailable offences in a serious economic fraud. Notice under s.446 CrPC issued to a surety who claimed he had merely signed the bonds as identifier.

Surety bond of Ichchhita Dungarwal (A-180) accepted; Neha Kataria (A-181) to appear on 03.10.2019.

contentions_and_observations: No contentions - adjournment only.

contentions_and_observations: No contentions recorded in this order.

The Jail Superintendent's written reply blamed an ACMM Jaipur order; the court rejected it as baseless, observing the ACMM had never directed the jail not to produce the accused elsewhere and had no authority to prevent their production before a Special Court of a Sessions Judge.
what_the_order_decided: Composite order across all 187 accused. Jail Superintendent's explanation for non-production of Rohit Modi (A-123) rejected as baseless; fresh production warrant for 03.10.2019 with copies to ACMM and SSP Jaipur and a warning of action against the police authorities. Fresh warrant of arrest against Sidharth Chauhan (A-135). Anticipatory bail of Praveen Maheshwari (A-156) and Rajeev Maheshwari (A-157) allowed. Twenty-one absent accused listed for 03.10.2019. Accused in custody remanded till 30.09.2019.

SFIO conceded at the bar that as to these six it was essentially a case of no evidence. Court relaxed and recalled the passport and travel conditions.
what_the_order_decided: Six accused furnished bail and surety bonds. The condition of surrendering passports and not leaving India was relaxed and recalled, the SFIO conceding it was essentially a case of no evidence against these six. Avanish Kumar Tyagi's affidavit of holding no passport accepted. All directed to appear on 03.10.2019.

scope_accused_affected: GENERAL - all 187 accused; specifically named: 2 (A-1, A-187)
contentions_and_observations: SFIO applied to correct clerical errors in the summoning order of 03.06.2019, explaining that in Para 9 some names had been omitted and others wrongly inserted through a copy-paste error while repeatedly pasting names - in particular A-115 to A-141 omitted from sub-para (I), companies omitted from (V), A-122 omitted from (VI), A-154 wrongly substituted for A-126 in (VII). Court applied the principle that an error apparent on the face of the record does not depend for its discovery on argument or disputation, and that a clerical error is a mistake in writing or typing, and allowed the correction, the discussion in the order having carried the correct details of their roles throughout.
what_the_order_decided: SFIO's application to correct clerical errors in the summoning order dated 03.06.2019 allowed. Names of accused and companies omitted or wrongly inserted in Para 9 sub-paras (I), (V), (VI), (VII) and (VIII) through a copy-paste error were corrected, and the corrected Para 9 (I) to (XX) was substituted and made part of the main order. (Order text dated 11.07.2019 although listed under 18.09.2019.)

contentions_and_observations: Twelve anticipatory bail applications part-heard and directed to be decided simultaneously as arising from the same facts. Court dismissed it: if he had genuinely shifted address 5-6 years earlier, his knowledge of the pendency of the complaint was unexplained; that knowledge showed he was aware of the proceedings and the application was filed merely to gain time, and was not maintainable absent surrender.
what_the_order_decided: Twelve anticipatory bail applications part-heard and directed to be decided simultaneously as arising from the same allegations. Application of Nitin Rathore (A-116) to cancel the warrant of arrest dismissed as not maintainable, he having declined to surrender; the court held his knowledge of the proceedings showed deliberate avoidance of service.

Counsel for A-155, A-163 to A-166 and A-170 to A-178 argued their clients' absence was covered by the court's own observations of 04.09.2019. Company representatives pleaded fever or being out of station; exemption was allowed for that day only, the court taking a lenient view while recording dissatisfaction with the grounds.

contentions_and_observations: On the medical condition of Surender Singh (A-140). contentions_and_observations: The most fully argued order in the set - 25 pages. Rajeev Kumar Rana (A-177) sought cancellation of the arrest warrant, arguing that he was never arrested during the investigation, which he had joined and cooperated with, and that under Siddharth v. State of U.P. and Aman Preet Singh v. CBI he could not be arrested now; he also relied on anticipatory bail granted to comparable accused by the Allahabad High Court and the Supreme Court, including to a co-accused in this very complaint. The Special Prosecutor replied that the case is governed by a special statute, that the application was not maintainable as anticipatory bail had been refused on 04.09.2019 and the challenge withdrawn on 01.10.2019, and that the court must additionally satisfy itself of the special statute's requirements over and above the CrPC. Court framed the question as whether non-arrest during investigation entitles an accused to immunity once process has issued, where anticipatory bail was refused and he has not appeared despite warrants. It held Aman Preet Singh and Siddharth distinguishable - neither dealt with s.212(6) of the Companies Act 2013, Aman Preet Singh turning on s.170 CrPC in an IPC case and Siddharth on anticipatory bail outside the Companies Act - and dismissed the application as a misuse of process seeking relief available only to an accused already on bail.
what_the_order_decided: Detailed twenty-five page order dismissing Rajeev Kumar Rana's application for cancellation of the non-bailable warrant and exemption from personal appearance. The court held that the Supreme Court's decisions in Aman Preet Singh v. CBI and Siddharth v. State of U.P. were distinguishable, neither having dealt with Section 212(6) of the Companies Act 2013, a special statute independent of the CrPC on the question of bail, and characterised the application as a misuse of process seeking relief available only to an accused already on bail.

what_the_order_decided: Detailed composite order with an important direction on the approvers. contentions_and_observations: A fully argued refusal of travel. Court dismissed it, holding that the purpose of the visit had been intentionally concealed, the application nowhere specifying any reason, which lent substance to the prosecution's apprehension.
what_the_order_decided: Application of Indu Tak for release of her passport and permission to travel to Vietnam from 07.05.2026 to 18.05.2026 dismissed. The SFIO opposed it, pointing to the seriousness of the financial fraud offences and a flight risk. The court held that the purpose of the visit had been intentionally concealed, the application nowhere specifying why she wished to travel, which lent force to the prosecution's apprehension.

what_the_order_decided: Tabular roll-call order culminating in proclamation proceedings. The court concluded that Mukesh Modi (A-113) and Rahul Virendra Modi (A-114) were evading its process and ordered a proclamation against them requiring their appearance on 08.10.2026, to be effected on or before 07.09.2026, more than thirty days in advance.
